claim: EVPI (expected payoff with perfect information minus best expected payoff now) is never negative and caps the value of any real test. A test that costs more than EVPI is never worth running.
agent_test: Unit test the routine on the 350 example, then count tests skipped by the EVPI cap at equal tokens versus an always-test arm.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Values of several tests are not additive; each is valued after updating on the others. Choose tests one at a time and recompute after each result.
agent_test: Compare one-at-a-time recompute against scoring a fixed batch up front on the same token budget.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: In theory a greedy one-step value of information can stop too early. Theorem 7 (Hay 2012): if the myopic rule continues, the optimal rule continues. (The LLM size of the look-ahead gain is a separate claim, K27.)
agent_test: Stop rule variants: one-step versus 3-test bundle. Same token cap, measure final accuracy.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Number of tests has a finite expected cap: E[N] <= EVPI/c (c = cost per step). Stopping is certain in theory but run length is unbounded, so a hard cap is still needed. Gap search: no LLM study tests an EVPI/c cap; the stop rules that exist are agreement-based (K29).
agent_test: Set step cap = min(hard cap, EVPI/c) and compare against fixed caps at equal total tokens.

claim: Selecting computations by value per cost beat a fixed plan in search: 64 percent win rate against UCT at 10000 samples per ply on 9x9 Go.
agent_test: Not directly testable on language tasks; test the principle with a value-per-cost chooser over thinking steps.

claim: Choosing questions by expected information gain computed in code, with the model only proposing candidates and wording, beats the model choosing its own question (20 Questions, diagnosis, code clarification, preference elicitation).
agent_test: Arm A model picks the test; arm B model proposes k and code ranks by EIG over an explicit hypothesis set. Same tokens.

claim: Size of the gain from information-driven questions: UoT +38.1 percent average success over direct prompting (5 datasets, 5 LLMs, 3 repeats); BED-LLM +37.4 points on 20 Questions; Kobalczyk +8 to +15 points on HumanEval and APPS after 4 rounds for weaker models.
agent_test: Reproduce on our own hypothesis-elimination tasks; report confidence intervals because UoT used only 3 repeats.

claim: The gain shrinks or vanishes with stronger models and in open-ended settings: GPT-4o-mini HumanEval binary gap 1.9 points (about 1 standard error); several UoT open-set cells under 3 points. Gap search adds: an EIG-reward-trained questioner gave x2 on Qwen2.5-7B but +4.2 and +1.8 points on 14B, and inference-time BED-LLM fell below the 14B baseline on Animals (26.4 vs 35.0); MedClarify gained +2.3 on GPT-5.1 versus +7.8 on DeepSeek-R1 and +4.9 on Llama-3.3-70B; the budget-control VOI gain was smaller on GPT-5.4-Mini than on Qwen3-32B.
agent_test: Measure the gain per model strength. Run info scoring only when the base asker is weak or the stakes are high.

claim: How EIG is estimated matters: EIG weighted by the model's own log-probabilities did worse than plain prompting in some models; uniform weighting was best. BED-LLM ablation: full EIG with filtering (86) beat entropy-only (64) on GPT-4o Celebrities.
agent_test: Compare uniform versus model-weighted hypothesis weights at equal samples.

claim: Raw LLM test proposals are often useless: 33 to 40 percent of valid sampled Battleship programs had zero EIG, and best-of-k selection by EIG reaches human-mean quality at k=5 and exceeds it at k=10.
agent_test: Count zero-information proposals in our own test lists; compare k=1, 5, 10 at fixed tokens. (a22, a23, c23 are the same paper.)

claim: Models do not know what is missing. QuestBench: Logic-Q and Planning-Q under 50 percent; models said not sure 0.7 to 4.6 percent of the time when 41.8 percent were truly underspecified. Filtering to solvable items did not fix it.
agent_test: Add a code-side step that enumerates unknowns; compare its detection rate with model self-report.

claim: Models answer early on assumptions in multi-turn settings instead of asking: average -39 percent across six tasks, 15 LLMs, 200,000+ simulated conversations.
agent_test: Force an ask-or-answer decision step and compare against free-form behaviour.

claim: Letting the model ask whenever it likes can hurt: MediQ direct asking cut accuracy 11.3 percent relative; a confidence gate recovered it (+22.3 percent over BASIC). Fixed-round questioning shows an inverted-U against rounds (Dong 2026).
agent_test: Test ungated, fixed-round and gated asking at equal tokens.

claim: Net-value rules (information value minus cost) match or beat tuned confidence thresholds without tuning: VoI won or tied in 18 of 20 conditions; Mixed 20Q at c=0.01 gave 14.14 versus 11.49. VoI kept asking in a high-stakes case and stopped early in a low-stakes one (one instance). Gap search: in a simulation the cost-aware ranker plus net-value stop beat a tuned entropy threshold by 33 points while stopping alone recovered at most 4 (d01); an LLM run of the same rule with a sampled-agreement proxy earned less than always retrieving (U 2.20 vs 5.33, d02). No study runs payoff gate, information-gain ranker and tuned threshold together at equal tokens.
agent_test: Replicate with two stake levels on our tasks, our VoI gate versus a confidence threshold tuned on a held-out split.

claim: Confidence is not value of information. Calibrating verbalized confidence changes which answers are committed to but does not show the benefit of another retrieval; overall accuracy ranged from +15 to -17 points. Contested: confidence-weighted agreement did stop sampling sooner at equal accuracy (ReASC, up to 70% cheaper, d17), but sampled agreement missed 5 of 5 confident wrong answers in the GPT-4.1 retrieval test (d02). Confidence helps to stop repeats; it does not give the value of a new kind of test.
agent_test: Check whether stated confidence predicts which items benefit from one more test (correlation with realized gain).

claim: Gating expensive checks by an uncertainty proxy for VoI saves tokens at equal or higher success: ALFWorld 78.3 percent at 56k tokens versus 74.2 at 341k always-on critique, both with online SFT.
agent_test: Gate a critic call by entropy and top-2 margin of the answer distribution; compare with always-on at matched tokens. The paper also fine-tunes the actor.

claim: Adding a per-token cost to reasoning reward cuts output length 23-45 percent at similar accuracy, more on easy items. Training-free sample-stopping rules agree: Adaptive-Consistency 3.3x fewer samples with under 0.1 percent accuracy loss; ESC 34-84 percent fewer.
agent_test: Run adaptive stopping of self-consistency against fixed N at equal token budget. (a17 and b25 are the same paper.)

claim: Estimating VoI itself costs compute and is biased: naive Monte Carlo EVPI is biased upward at small samples; nested EIG estimators are biased at any finite inner size; regression shortcuts cut 55 minutes to seconds but fail with many parameters or correlated inputs.
schema_part: S4 (keep scoring cheap, over a few named unknowns)
agent_test: Measure rank stability of test scores across resamples; scoring must cost far less than the tests.

claim: The belief inputs to VoI are weak in LLMs: off-the-shelf models update beliefs poorly across turns; stated probabilities were only fairly calibrated (worse in medical); LLM bandit exploration fails without outside summaries.
schema_part: G5/memory (store beliefs outside the model, update in code)
agent_test: Keep an explicit candidate list with code-side Bayes updates versus model-held beliefs.

claim: Humans do not choose tests by the textbook measure. Probability gain (expected error reduction) explained human search best in three experiments; people also seek non-instrumental information and sometimes avoid useful free information, so the never-negative rule fails for real motives. Gap search: still no LLM study compares information gain with probability gain; BED-LLM shows a halving (Split) rule gets most of the gain with an explicit candidate set (K09, d10).
schema_part: S4 (probability gain as an alternative score)
agent_test: Compare ranking by information gain versus probability gain on our tasks; they disagree on specific cases.

claim: Information-gain score alone ignores payoff and cost: UoT has no cost term; EIG measures reduced uncertainty, not decision value; Kobalczyk lists U=EIG-c but ranks by EIG. Pair a cheap EIG ranker with a payoff-based EVPI gate.
agent_test: Two-stage design versus EIG-only; measure tests per solved item.

claim: Training a model to ask better (EIG rewards, DPO, STaR-GATE) improves question quality, but gains are partial: BigBench success rose 17.2 to 31.0 while EIG fell 0.31 to 0.28.
agent_test: Not for the scaffold; use as an upper reference for what a prompt-only ranker should reach.

claim: Decision-theory scaffolds (list states, forecast, elicit utilities, maximise expected utility) beat direct and CoT prompting, up to 40 percent accuracy gain, but have no question-asking step.
agent_test: Apply an explicit expected-utility step to test choice versus plain CoT.

claim: Calibrated ask-or-act sets (conformal prediction) cut human help 10-24 percent at a fixed success target, but need exchangeable calibration data.
agent_test: Calibrate an ask threshold on a held-out split; check coverage on a shifted set.

claim: In health economics EVPI above research cost is necessary but not sufficient for recommending research; of 86 articles, 66 recommended research and no tested covariate predicted it.
agent_test: None needed; design hint only. Only abstract-level reading.

claim: Bayesian multi-LLM orchestration reported 34 percent lower cost; figures unverified (single author, attribution percentages sum to 114).
agent_test: Do not rely on it.

claim: Look-ahead beats one-step selection in LLM test choice by a very large margin when tests pay off only in combination (Cube-NM: 75.0 vs 30.2 percent after five tests, two-step vs one-step, small Qwen3-0.6B model), but by a small margin in a natural task (target prediction at turn 5: 32.7 for K=3, 30.8 for K=2, 29.7 for K=1). A depth-2 conversation tree raised success 21.8 points over direct prompting at +1.8 turns (CA-BED). No study ablates depth in natural tasks or reports the token price.
agent_test: Use depth 1 by default. Use depth 2 only when two tests are known to be complementary. Measure tokens per point gained.

claim: With an open target space, a cheap recipe works for entities the model can name: sample hypotheses from the LLM, reject those that conflict with past answers, keep survivors, ask for diverse batches, weight evenly (BED-LLM: ICL belief tracking instead gave 25 vs 93 on Animals GPT-4o). Model-discovery work keeps a capped pool (24) and grows it only when a fit check fails. Nobody measures how often the true answer is missing from the set or how wrong the set can be before EIG ranking turns harmful.
agent_test: Log whether the final answer was ever in the hypothesis set. Add an explicit 'none of these' hypothesis and test whether the agent asks a broadening question when its fit check fails.

claim: Agreement-based stop rules for repeated samples save a lot with little accuracy loss on easy and medium items: Adaptive-Consistency up to 7.9x fewer samples, under 0.1% loss; ESC -33.8% (MATH) to -84.2% (Coin Flip); CGES -58% calls (16.0 to 6.7) for -0.4 points; Certified SC about 61 to 86 of 100 samples with a valid error bound; CoT+program agreement 9.3x fewer samples, 78.6% done in two. They save least on hard items (MATH -33.8%, GPQA -2.1 points with little saving), and none compares to a value-based EVPI/c stop.
schema_part: S7 stop rule / G7 hard cap
agent_test: Stop on posterior >= threshold with a hard cap of 16. Add the EVPI/c cap as a second arm and compare at equal total tokens.

claim: More questions or tests have an interior optimum: clarification success peaked at a middle budget and fell or flattened beyond it (tau-bench), the trained clarifier asked 1.3 questions against 3.9-5.1 for general models, and a forced fixed number of costly tests (K=3) did worse than greedy in simulation (50.92 vs 56.76). Hard caps near 10 turns are used in practice (MedClarify).
agent_test: Set a question cap of 1-3 for clarification and test caps of 2, 4 and 8 for evidence checks; plot success against cap.

claim: Turning on reasoning in the base model did not make it a better questioner: final 20 Questions solve rate fell in every category with reasoning on, and QuestBench models (including o1-preview and Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking) said 'not sure' on 0.7-4.6% of Planning-Q cases where the true rate was 41.8%. Evidence covers models up to 2025; Gemini 2.5 Pro appears only in qualitative traces. No clean test with 2026 reasoning models.
agent_test: Do not rely on the model to say what is missing. Force a checklist of required slots and count unfilled slots in code.

claim: LLM-elicited payoff tables are noisy but usable: pairwise utility rankings agreed with human labels 65.3-70.4%; a decision-theory scaffold got 73.3% / 64.2% against o1-preview 33.3% / 35.0%. A sampled-agreement belief proxy missed confident wrong answers (5 of 5 zero-entropy cases wrong). No study tests whether an LLM-elicited EVPI predicts the realized gain of one more test.
agent_test: Record predicted gain before each test and realized gain after. Report the correlation. Show VOI as a range, not a point.

claim: The value of a check depends on the loss from a wrong answer, so gates should be stake-weighted: a read-only verifier rejected 61% of invalid episodes while withholding 17% of valid ones at under one cent per episode, and whether planning or verification mattered more flipped with the assigned liability; the VOI rule asked longer at reward 10 than at reward 1 (one instance).
agent_test: Give each task a stake weight. Run the verifier when stake x error rate exceeds its cost.

claim: Nonadditivity of VOI across tests and the failure of simple formulas for risk-averse decision makers are stated in secondary sources only. Howard 1966 (five pages) and Raiffa-Schlaifer 1961 were not opened, so what they prove about the risk-averse case is unverified here. For an agent maximising expected accuracy (risk neutral) the textbook formulas apply.
agent_test: State the risk-neutral assumption in the schema. Do not claim results for risk-averse payoffs.
